subject: Post-call: SLO validation & customer-led throughput runbook (QuantifyAI)
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Noor <samira@quantify.ai>, James Liu <james.liu@quantify.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: SLO validation & customer-led throughput runbook (QuantifyAI)

Hi Samira / James —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can get your customer-led run completed smoothly: 

Summary of SLOs you asked us to validate:
- P95 token latency for chat-style generation: <= 220ms (short prompts, batching 1)
- Sustained throughput: 500 requests/sec (avg req = 80 tokens)
- Concurrent streaming connections: up to 120 persistent client streams
- Recovery objective: service fallback to smaller model variant within 30s on degraded nodes

What Redwood will provide next: 
- A focused runbook for customer-led testing (attached: redwood_slo_runbook_v1.pdf) with step-by-step k6 and Locust snippets.
- A scoped, short-lived test API key scoped to the QuantifyAI sandbox project.
- An IP allowlist template (attached) — provide your egress IPs and we’ll add them to the tenant allowlist.

Action items for QuantifyAI: 
1) Confirm a 2–4 hour test window in the week of Apr 26–30 (we propose Apr 27 02:00–06:00 PT or Apr 29 22:00–02:00 PT).
2) Provide an account email for the test key and any static egress IPs you will use (or confirm you’ll use our staged runner).
3) Tell us whether you prefer k6 or Locust for your main script; we’ll share tuned examples for both.

Neha (SE) — I’ve asked you to draft the example k6 script and highlight token-scoping steps; Vivek — please pre-author the allowlist entries and monitoring links.

Samira, if you can reply with preferred window and toolchain we’ll lock in the engineering standby.

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
pri.yom@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0199

Attachments: redwood_slo_runbook_v1.pdf, sample_k6_script.js, ip_allowlist_template.csv
From: Samira Noor <samira@quantify.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: James Liu <james.liu@quantify.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: SLO validation & customer-led throughput runbook (QuantifyAI)

Thanks Priyom — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We want the streaming tests to exercise partial-output streaming (line-delimited events) for ~60% of requests; the rest are standard generation.
- Target concurrency for streaming: 120 persistent websockets, peak ramping to 200 for short bursts.
- Sustained synthetic traffic: aiming for 500 rps for 90 minutes, with two short 5-minute spikes to 1200 rps to validate autoscaling behavior.

We’ll use k6 for the main run but have an internal Locust harness for streaming; please include both examples.

For the test window we prefer Apr 29 22:00–02:00 PT (that avoids our daytime). Please issue the test key to qa+stress@quantify.ai. Our network will egress from these CIDRs: 34.82.10.0/24 and 34.82.11.0/24.

Also — do you have guidance on per-connection idle timeouts and max simultaneous sessions per backend instance? We need to sanity-check our Locust worker sizing.

Samira
Head of Platform | QuantifyAI
samira@quantify.ai

Subject: Re: Post-call: SLO validation & customer-led throughput runbook (QuantifyAI)

Hi Samira —

Great — k6 + Locust both supported. Answers and what we’ll provision: 

1) Test key and scoping
- We will provision a scoped test API key for qa+stress@quantify.ai valid for 48 hours. It will be limited to the sandbox tenant and capped at 1500 rps to prevent accidental overrun.

2) IP allowlist
- We’ll add 34.82.10.0/24 and 34.82.11.0/24 to the tenant allowlist. Please confirm if any additional NATed egress ranges exist. Attached is an ip_allowlist_template.csv you can return with any extras.

3) Streaming and connection guidance
- Backend connection idle timeout: 90s by default; we can extend to 300s for the run if you expect long-lived streams.
- Max simultaneous backend sessions per model instance: default is 60; for your target 120 persistent streams we’ll route across multiple instances; expect >2 instances to be utilized at steady state.
- For short spike bursts (to 1200 rps) we recommend pre-warming with a 10-minute ramp and enabling burst capacity — we’ll open a temporary burst pool for the test window.

4) Locust sizing notes
- Use 4–6 workers per 100 simulated streaming clients for stable throughput; tune worker spawn rates to avoid sudden client flood.

5) Monitoring & observability
- We’ll provide per-route latency dashboards and a token-level cost heatmap. Link to the temporary monitoring dashboard will be shared when the window is locked.

Proposed confirmation: Apr 29 22:00–02:00 PT (we’ll provision test key and allowlist 4 hours prior). If that works we’ll send the test key and monitoring link 2 hours before start.

Attaching: sample_k6_script.js and the ip_allowlist_template.csv.

-Neha

Vivek will post the monitoring link and a Slack escalation channel (we’ll include on-call infra). Neha — thanks for the script edits. Samira — we’ll send the test key and monitoring link per the timeline above.

Looking forward — Priyom
